log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 37% BRING: dragapult, 32% BRING: toxapex, 14% BRING: garchomp
Pick 2: 61% BRING: toxapex, 16% BRING: scizor, 14% BRING: garchomp
Pick 3: 53% BRING: scizor, 29% BRING: garchomp, 10% BRING: chandelure

Plan: lead Incineroar for Fake Out and Intimidate support. Garchomp is the mega threat for sweeping later. Gholdengo covers special attacks and Scizor. Watch for Dragapult (fast, Infiltrator) and Chandelure's special power. Toxapex is a wall; use Garchomp or Gholdengo to break it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Looking at the opponent's lineup against my team, I'm weighing Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as my three picks, considering Gholdengo's strength as a check to several of their threats.

decisions.thought: 28% SWITCH: scizor, 26% MOVE: uturn, 17% SWITCH: toxapex

Lead Incineroar vs Dragapult (Dragon/Ghost). Fake Out is useless here (Ghost immune). Intimidate already dropped Dragapult's Atk. Dragapult is likely faster than everything I have except possibly Garchomp; it may be Infiltrator/Cursed Body. Use Flare Blitz for damage now. Garchomp (Mega threat, Swords Dance) is my sweeper later. Gholdengo handles Scizor/Toxapex-type Steel/Poison targets. Opponent still has Toxapex, Scizor, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, Chandelure to come.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Fake Out won't work since Dragapult is Ghost-type and immune to Normal moves. Flare Blitz is also weakened since Fire is resisted by Dragon, though neutral against Ghost.

Weighing options: Protect feels wasteful here, while Parting Shot to pivot into Garchomp is tempting but speed is uncertain. Flare Blitz still seems like the most reliable damage option despite the recoil, so I'll go with that.

decisions.thought: 40% MOVE: uturn, 31% SWITCH: toxapex, 15% MOVE: dragonclaw

Dragapult (Dragon/Ghost) is faster and resists Flare Blitz, so Incineroar's attack is weak here. Parting Shot lowers its Atk and SpA and brings in Gholdengo, which has Shadow Ball (super effective on Dragapult) and resists its Dragon moves. Garchomp is the later sweeper with Swords Dance once Dragapult is handled. Watch for Toxapex, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, or Chandelure as the last opponent.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since Dragapult resists Fire, Flare Blitz isn't great here, and it's faster with strong special attacks like Draco Meteor or Shadow Ball. I'm weighing switching Incineroar out for Garchomp, which shares Dragon typing but adds Ground coverage.

Against Gholdengo, Dragapult's Dragon moves are resisted while Ghost moves hit super effectively, so Shadow Ball or Phantom Force are the better attacking options. Alternatively, Incineroar could use Parting Shot to drop Dragapult's Atk and SpA further while safely switching in Gholdengo.

I'll go with Parting Shot — it keeps the pivot option open and cripples the incoming threat's offenses.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Incineroar was forced out by Parting Shot. Opponent has Toxapex (-1 Atk, -1 SpA) active. Dragapult, Scizor (fainted) seen; Dragapult has U-turn. Garchomp is the mega sweeper later, with Swords Dance and Earthquake hitting Toxapex super effectively. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks Toxapex's status moves like Toxic, so it switches in safely and hits Toxapex with Thunderbolt. Plan: Gholdengo breaks Toxapex, then Garchomp sweeps.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's forced out, likely from Parting Shot, so my only options are switching to Garchomp or Gholdengo against the active Toxapex with its lowered attack stats.

Electric moves hit Toxapex hard thanks to its Water typing, so Gholdengo's Thunderbolt is a solid option, but Garchomp's Earthquake is super effective too given Toxapex's Poison/Water typing, and Garchomp's speed lets it strike first. The tradeoff is that Garchomp would be exposed to Toxic or Scald if it switches in, so I'm weighing whether Gholdengo is the safer pick.

decisions.thought: 39% MOVE: toxicspikes, 38% SWITCH: dragapult, 16% MOVE: toxic

Gholdengo (Life Orb, Good as Gold) is active and outspeeds Toxapex. Good as Gold blocks Toxapex's status moves, so it can attack freely. Thunderbolt is super effective on Toxapex (Water). Opponent has Dragapult (U-turn, fast, maybe Infiltrator/Cursed Body), Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Chandelure left. Garchomp (Mega) is my late sweeper. Incineroar is at 52% with Sitrus Berry. Watch for Toxapex Regenerator switching.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Gholdengo already boosted and Toxapex at -1/-1, Thunderbolt hits it hard since it's part Water, though I'm also weighing whether Nasty Plot first would be better since Good as Gold blocks status moves against me anyway.

decisions.thought: 41% SWITCH: dragapult, 25% MOVE: recover, 19% MOVE: toxic

Gholdengo (Life Orb, Good as Gold, faster than Toxapex) should KO the 41% Toxapex with Thunderbolt, which is super effective. Toxapex may have Regenerator, so if it switches out it heals a third. Dragapult (U-turn, fast, possibly Infiltrator or Cursed Body) and Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Chandelure remain. Plan: Garchomp (Mega, Swords Dance) is the late sweeper. Keep Gholdengo for Dragapult/Rotom only if safe, and watch Toxic Spikes on my side.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Toxapex is at 41% HP, and since Gholdengo outspeeds, I'm checking if Thunderbolt is super effective on the Poison/Water typing—it should be, and likely enough to knock it out given the remaining HP.

decisions.thought: 49% MOVE: shadowball, 26% MOVE: phantomforce, 15% SWITCH: toxapex

Gholdengo (Life Orb, Good as Gold) is active at 132/164. Opposing Dragapult is at 70% and has U-turn; its ability is unknown (Clear Body, Infiltrator, or Cursed Body). Toxapex (Regenerator, Toxic Spikes) is likely to come back later. Shadow Ball is super effective on Dragapult's Ghost typing, so I'm using it now. Garchomp (Mega, Swords Dance) remains my late sweeper. Incineroar is at 52% with Sitrus Berry, and Parting Shot is useful for scouting or switching. Rotom-Wash and Chandelure are still unseen.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the current battle state—Gholdengo at 132/164 and Dragapult at 70% HP, trying to work out whether Shadow Ball is super effective against Dragapult's Dragon/Ghost typing.

Shadow Ball with Gholdengo's high Special Attack and STAB should hit hard here, likely enough to threaten a KO on Dragapult's remaining ~126 HP, so that's the move I'll go with.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo fainted to Dragapult's Shadow Ball, but Dragapult fainted too. Remaining opposing threats: Toxapex (100%, Regenerator, Leftovers, has set Toxic Spikes), Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, Chandelure. Switching in full-HP Garchomp: Earthquake is super effective on Toxapex. Mega Garchomp with Swords Dance is my late sweeper. Incineroar at 52% stays in reserve for Parting Shot or Fake Out. Watch for Toxapex switching to heal.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Gholdengo down, I'm weighing Garchomp against Incineroar to face the fully healed Toxapex, noting Garchomp's Ground typing gives it a super-effective Earthquake option against the Poison/Water type.

Incineroar isn't really needed here since Garchomp handles it better, but Mega Evolution isn't available this turn, likely since this is a forced switch after Gholdengo fainted. So the right move is just to switch in Garchomp normally.

decisions.thought: 66% MOVE: toxic, 12% MOVE: recover, 12% MOVE: toxicspikes

Gholdengo fell to Dragapult, which is down. Garchomp (full HP, poisoned, faster than Toxapex) now faces Toxapex at 74%. Mega Garchomp with Earthquake should KO it, since Ground is super effective on Poison. Toxapex's Regenerator heals only on switch-out, so a switch would bring it back to about 74% plus a third. Remaining opposing threats: Rotom-Wash, Garchomp (possibly Sand Veil or Rough Skin), Chandelure. Incineroar (52%) is in reserve for Parting Shot or Fake Out. Watch for Toxapex switching to heal.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp outspeeds Toxapex and Earthquake hits it super effectively since it's Poison/Water, though Toxapex's huge Defense will cushion the blow considerably.

Garchomp is already poisoned, so that extra chip damage isn't a big deal. After Toxapex falls, I'd be looking at Rotom-Wash, their own Garchomp, and Chandelure next, and Mega evolving now still seems fine given Mega Garchomp's stats stay strong on both offense and speed.
